intro.title: Experiments, run in the open.
intro.lead: The Lab is where new tools start. Each one begins with a question, is built in the open and is run with real people. Then it either graduates into a product or is written up and retired.

protocol.title: Question
protocol.body: Every experiment starts with one thing we want to find out, written down before any code.

protocol.title: Build in the open
protocol.body: The source is public from the first release, under an open licence anyone can read and reuse.

protocol.title: Run with people
protocol.body: A working version runs on our lab servers. Anyone can use it, and every finding is welcome.

protocol.title: Graduate or retire
protocol.body: If it earns its place, it becomes a product we look after. If not, we say what we learned and wind it down with notice.

rules.title: Expect change
rules.body: Lab tools move fast. Features can change from one week to the next, and we note what changed in each release.

rules.title: Private by design
rules.body: No accounts unless an experiment truly needs them, no tracking, and as little data on our servers as the tool allows.

rules.title: Findings in public
rules.body: Bugs, ideas and objections go to the experiment's public issue tracker, so everyone can see what was reported and what we did about it.

experiments.name: Rondel
experiments.question: Can a team run its retros and everyday meetings without accounts, with nothing readable on the server?
experiments.summary: Write, group, vote, discuss and agree actions in a retro, or run a meeting with an agenda, timer, shared notes, decisions and action items. Prepare before it starts, and repeat it weekly or monthly from one link. Everything people write is encrypted in the browser with a key that lives only in the meeting link.

setup.label: Encryption
setup.value: End to end, in the browser

setup.label: Self-hosting
setup.value: Cloudflare, Node, Docker or static files

experiments.name: Kunla
experiments.kind: Record of work for people and AI agents
experiments.question: Can a team's AI agents keep the record of their own work, so people only see the decisions that need them?
experiments.summary: Every person and every AI connection is a team member. Agents claim tasks, log progress and submit work themselves over MCP, from Claude Code, claude.ai, Codex or any other agent. People get one short inbox of reviews, questions and proposals, and a correction can become a rule sent to every agent with its next task.
